Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
252 PM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Thursday's system continues to trend drier for most of the area
with precipitation chances increasing to NE MD. Continue to
monitor mountain snow later this week. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Rain returns Thursday as colder temperatures follow Friday
 into the weekend, with mountain snow and brisk conditions.

- 2) Cooler temperatures & dry condtions expected for much of
  next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Rain returns Thursday as colder temperatures follow Friday
 into the weekend, with mountain snow and brisk conditions.

Dry and warm conditions continue this afternoon ahead of a
strong cold front impacting the forecast area on Thursday. A low
pressure system tracking from the Ohio River Valley and into the
Mid-Atlantic pushes the associated cold front across the area 
on Thursday. Precipitation moves into the Alleghenies early 
Thursday morning before tracking east through the day. QPF 
associated with this system has overall trended downward with 
much of the area receiving a trace to a few tenths of an inch of
precip at most. Behind the front, brisk conditions are expected
as winds gust around 20mph and high temperatures stay in the 
40s and 50s on Friday and Saturday. 

The Alleghenies can expected to see their first accumulating
snowfall as northwest winds bring upslope snow showers to the
region. Light snowfall begins Thursday night as temperatures
fall below freezing and continue through the day on Friday.
Marginal temperatures likely limit accumulations during the day
on Friday to the highest ridges where temperatures remain below
freezing.Overall, the best chance for accumulating snow is 
Friday night which could result in travel disruptions as 
surfaces get covered. Temperatures fall into the 20s and 30s 
Friday night. Total accumulations are expected to remain below 
Winter Weather Advisory criteria at this time. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler temperatures & dry condtions expected 
for much of next week. 

As the weekend's longwave trough slowly pushes offshore early next 
week, winds could remain elevated through Sunday before diminishing 
between Monday & Tuesday in the wake of the cold front. Temperatures 
are likely to remain much cooler areawide throughout the week, with 
many areas seeing near or below freezing temperatures overnight 
beginning this weekend through the remainder of the forecast period.

Overall, generally calm, clear conditions persist throughout the 
week as a upper-level ridging transitions overhead. Daytime 
temperatures moderate a bit later in the week with continued high 
pressure, with afternoon highs in the mid-to-upper 50s on
Wednesday. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
VFR conditions continue this afternoon with light winds blowing
out of the south. Cloud cover increases overnight as a cold
front approaches. Light rain is expected across the terminals on
Thursday, with MVFR conditions possible with reduced ceilings. 

In the wake of the front, winds shift to northwesterly Thursday
evening gusting up to 30 knots. VFR conditions return Friday 
with winds gusting 20 to 25 knots each day. 

Northwest winds could gust up to 25-30 knots between Saturday and 
Sunday in the wake of a cold front. Otherwise, VFR conditions are 
expected through the weekend. Winds diminish by early next week, 
shifting northerly by Tuesday. 

&&

.MARINE...
Light winds continue this afternoon and into the overnight with
non hazardous conditions expected over the waters. In the wake
of a strong cold front, winds shift to northwesterly with SCA
conditions likely through the weekend. 

Winds likely remain within SCA thresholds through the weekend as the 
cold front passes offshore. Winds likely start to diminish between 
Sunday and Monday, shifting more northerly by Tuesday. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Action Stages are likely Thursday night before winds shift to 
northwest behind a cold front. A strong frontal passage will 
bring a prolonged period of blowout tides Friday and through 
early next week.
